title: A binary or map column is carried unchanged through project, filter, join, sort, UNION ALL and LIMIT
verdict: values and types arrive as read; IS NULL is exact
description: A binary column and a map column read from a table arrive unchanged after a projection, a filter on another column, an inner join on another column, a sort on another column, a UNION ALL and a LIMIT: every value equal, NULL included, for the binary values b'ab', NULL, the empty value, one zero byte and a 1 MiB value, and the maps [(a, 1)], NULL, the empty map, [('z\x00', 0)] and one of 1,000 entries (map<string, int64>). IS NULL is true exactly for the NULL rows.
The output types are BINARY (Arrow binary) and MAP(VARCHAR, BIGINT) (Arrow map<string, int64>), the input's.
reference: D67 (ruling 187): a column of a type the model does not read is opaque, carried and never read; the model holds an image of its value, and a well-kinded plan reads nothing from it. This fact is K7's evidence that the engine carries such a column unchanged.

provenance.checked_by: types-casts session (duckdb 2.0.0 in Python 3.12, macOS arm64, tables registered from Arrow), for ruling 187 K7

evidence.sql: SQL: SELECT id, b, m FROM t [WHERE id > 0 | JOIN u ON t.id = u.id | ORDER BY id DESC | ... UNION ALL ... | LIMIT 10]
evidence.observed: all six operations: every row equal to the input row (by id); IS NULL true only for id 2

provenance.notes: Probe: id 1..5 with the binary and map values listed in the description, joined with u(id, x) on id.
